summary: AVATAR-Synthetic is an AI-powered medical decision-support prototype for astronauts on deep-space missions. When an astronaut becomes ill, real organ-chip data (like NASA's AVATAR investigation) is unavailable in real time, and communication delays prevent immediate guidance from Earth. Our system fills this gap using three distinct layers: (real public NASA OSDR gene-expression data to train a Variational Autoencoder, real astronaut input (symptoms, vitals, genetics), and a computationally generated "synthetic chip profile" clearly labeled as an estimate, never a measurement. The system predicts biological vulnerability (immune suppression, radiation stress) and independent clinical risk from symptoms, combining them into a decision recommendation with a pre-written protocol. Every output includes an explicit confidence level; when data is insufficient, the model abstains. We do not diagnose or prescribe. We support decisions under uncertainty, honestly.
details:
AVATAR-Synthetic is a Streamlit-based decision-support dashboard. It works in three steps: (1) The astronaut inputs a profile (symptoms, vitals); the system computes a data-completeness score. (2) A VAE trained on NASA OSDR data generates a synthetic gene-expression profile, labeled with a confidence score (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH). (3) A Random Forest estimates biological vulnerability (0-100 scores for immune suppression, radiation stress, resilience), while an independent XGBoost model predicts clinical risk from symptoms only. A hard-coded decision layer combines both tracks into a recommendation with a pre-written protocol. The project is creative because it explicitly separates real data from generated estimates, and it prioritizes honest uncertainty over false confidence.

Data Sources: NASA OSDR (public spaceflight gene-expression data) for training the VAE and biological models. DDXPlus (synthetic symptom dataset from Mila-Quebec) for training the clinical risk model. No other datasets were used.

Tools: Python, Streamlit, PyTorch, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, SHAP, Pandas, NumPy.

Ethical Considerations: The system never diagnoses disease, never prescribes medication, and never claims clinical validation. All synthetic outputs are labeled "SYNTHETIC" in the UI. When data completeness is below 40%, the model abstains and reports "INSUFFICIENT DATA." A qualified medical professional and mission protocols remain authoritative.
